A Nurturing School where every child can Learn, Thrive, and Belong.
Welcome to Robin’s Way School
At Robins Way, we believe every child deserves a safe, nurturing, and inspiring place to grow. As a school dedicated to supporting primary-aged pupils with social, emotional, and mental health (SEMH) needs, we are proud to provide a caring environment where every child is seen, heard, and valued.
Our team is passionate about helping each learner develop the confidence, resilience, and skills they need to thrive-both in school and beyond. We celebrate every small step of progress and tailor our approach to support the individual journeys of our pupils.
As Headteacher, I am deeply committed to working alongside families, professionals, and our dedicated staff to ensure that Robins Way is not just a school, but a community where children can truly flourish.
Jemma Taylor Headteacher
Curriculum
We provide nurturing classes that focus on the individual child and develop positive trusting relationships.
Clinical Therapy
As well as delivering the best possible education, we also have access to a clinical team who provide care and therapy to benefit our pupils.
Parent and carer Comments
I just wanted to offer some positive feedback. At home we have noticed a huge difference in J’s presentation and his new found love for school. Over the course of the school holiday recently we had friends and family over who were shocked at the change in J. They complimented how much calmer he seems since starting his new school and was excited to tell them about his friends, his teachers and his school which previously he would never talk about. He was also able to regulate himself far quicker than we have seen previously. We honestly cannot thank you all enough for the work you have done in such a short time and the work you continue to do with J.
Thank you, we really appreciate everything you’re all doing for H.
Thank you so much for your message. I’m very proud of my son and so pleased to hear that he had such a positive day and set a great example for others. I really appreciate you taking the time to let me know, it means a lot and thank you for all your hard work.
T enthusiastically told us about school today and this is the first time managing to accurately provide coherent feedback that aligns with what actually happened (not just at school, but ever). This is a huge thing and massive progress, we usually have to try and unlock the reality from the fantasy and her closing off, so thank you so much!!!

Home About Us Meet Our Team
Headteacher – Jemma Taylor
It is an honour to introduce myself as the Headteacher of Robin’s Way. I am originally from Northern Ireland and bring with me not just experience, but a deep personal understanding of the challenges some young people face. Having grown up with both Dyslexia and Dyscalculia, I know what it feels like to navigate education differently. That insight shapes my commitment to ensuring every pupil feels seen, understood, and supported.
I first trained as a Sports Therapist, but my journey into education began when I joined an
SEMH school in Blackburn as a Learning Support Assistant. It was there that I trained to become a Science teacher and discovered a passion for working with young people who need school to be more than just lessons, it must be a place of safety, structure, and trust. I later moved to Wiltshire to continue working within the SEN sector, completing my NPQH in September 2024. I served as Deputy Head at an SEMH school in Shaftesbury for two years before taking up the role here at Robin’s Way.
My core belief is simple: every person in a school, child or adult, deserves to feel safe, happy, and like they belong. I aim to lead with compassion, clarity, and high expectations. Robin’s Way will be a place where individuals are nurtured and empowered, where challenges are met with kindness and consistency, and where every success, big or small, is celebrated.
Outside of school, I’m a proud parent to my young son, Ethan, and enjoy spending time with my family. You’ll also meet Quill, our friendly school dog, who plays a big part in daily life at Robin’s Way. In my downtime, I enjoy rugby, golf, and perhaps unexpectedly, crochet, which gives me a moment of calm and creativity.
Together with our dedicated staff, supportive families, and resilient pupils, I’m excited for the future we’re building, one where everyone can thrive.
Deputy Headteacher – John Murphy
My name is John Murphy, and I am delighted to have been appointed Deputy Head at Robin’s Way School.
I hold a BEd (Hons) degree and originally qualified as a Teacher of Physical Education, with additional studies in SEN and Psychology. Over the past twenty-four years, I have worked extensively in mainstream secondary education, holding a variety of leadership roles including Assistant Head (Staff Development), Head of Faculty, Director of Maths, Director of Key Stage 4, and Year Head for Years 8–11.
My move into Special Education was driven by a strong desire to support some of the most vulnerable young people in our society. Since then, I’ve worked in two Pupil Referral Units (PRUs) as Maths Lead, Behaviour Lead, and Deputy Head. Most recently, I’ve spent seven years in the private independent sector as a Maths Lead, and prior to joining Robin’s Way, I was Head of School at a Hampshire-based setting for two and a half years.
Outside of school, I enjoy spending time with my three daughters and grandchildren, walking Luna, my energetic three-year-old German Shepherd and taking on DIY projects. My most recent creation, a pergola which last time I looked, it was still standing! I’m also a passionate Crystal Palace supporter and regularly travel the country to follow the team. I enjoy watching non-league football just as much.
I’m approachable and always happy to answer any questions you may have. I’m genuinely excited by the opportunity to work alongside Jemma Taylor (Headteacher), our fantastic staff team, and most importantly our pupils. I am fully committed to ensuring Robin’s Way is not only a place of learning, but a place where every young person can grow in confidence, character, and joy.
Clinical Lead – Karima Lovell
I am passionate about supporting children and the adults in their lives to thrive.
I have extensive experience working as a HCPC registered Dramatherapist in schools, the NHS and third sector organisations.
I am dedicated to supporting the embedding of truly trauma informed practice at Robins Way, aiming to ensure that the school environment feels safe, inclusive and person-centred for all.
SENCo – Cheryl Palmer
Hi, I am Cheryl, and I am delighted to be part of Robin’s Way as the SENCo, especially as the school continues to grow and develop. I am a trained primary school teacher and have worked in education for over ten years.
Before joining Robins Way, I spent several years working in an outdoor nursery, where I developed a deep appreciation for the rich learning opportunities that come from exploring the natural world. These experiences have shaped my belief that children thrive when they are supported to follow their interests, discover through play, and learn in environments that nurture their curiosity.
I am really looking forward to building strong, positive relationships with all of our pupils, their families, and the professionals we work alongside. By working together, I believe we can ensure every child is supported to achieve their fullest potential and feels confident, valued, and safe.
Outside of school, my life is wonderfully busy with my husband and our two young children, Charlie and Colby. I love spending time making memories with them, whether it’s watching my eldest play football or enjoying family days out together. In my spare time, I also love listening to music and enjoy going to the theatre to see musicals and attending concerts.
Assistant Head – Katie Stanley
Hi, I’m Katie Stanley and I’m really excited to be starting as the Assistant Head Teacher at Robin’s Way. I’ve been teaching for over 12 years, mostly in primary schools, and a few years ago I moved from mainstream education into SEN because it’s something I feel really passionate about.
For me, it’s so important that young children get a well-rounded, holistic education where we focus on personal development, build positive relationships, and still have lots of fun while learning. I’m really looking forward to working with the team to create a supportive and engaging environment that our young people enjoy being part of and look forward to coming into every day.
Outside of work, I love spending time walking my two dogs, Bear and Mila, catching up with friends and family, and generally being out and about whenever I can. I’m feeling really positive about the future of Robin’s Way and all the young lives we can support and make a difference to together.
School Business Manager – Charlie Mallett
With a background rooted in military life and public service, I bring a calm, resilient, and highly organised approach to my role at Robin’s Way School. After serving in the military and later supporting my husband through his own service, I built a varied career across the NHS and early years settings, working in administrative roles that strengthened my skills in communication, safeguarding processes, and family support.
Joining Robin’s Way marked a new chapter for me, and stepping into management has been an exciting challenge that I’m embracing wholeheartedly. I’m passionate about creating a nurturing, structured environment where every child can thrive, and I have a particular interest in SEND, ensuring that all pupils feel understood, supported, and celebrated.
Outside of school, I’m happiest outdoors with my family. I love spending time with my husband and son, walking with our much‑loved old dog Arty, and caring for my 31‑year‑old Pony, who has been part of my life for decades. Whether it’s a quiet countryside walk or time at the stables, being outdoors keeps me grounded and energised.

Home About Us What we do
At Robin’s Way School, we provide education for children aged 7 to 11 with Social, Emotional and Mental Health needs.
Our mission is straightforward: to equip every child with the skills, knowledge, and confidence they need to thrive in the future.
We understand that many of our pupils have faced challenges in their educational journey, which is why we take a creative and flexible approach to teaching.
Instead of focusing on obstacles, we see the potential in every pupil. By dedicating time to understanding each child’s individual needs, we design tailored support packages that enable them to succeed.
Our commitment extends beyond academic preparation—we focus on helping pupils grow socially and emotionally, ensuring they are ready to embrace the next stage of their lives with confidence. We encourage all our pupils to aim high and achieve their best in every aspect of their development. Our staff team are passionate about supporting our pupils, who will benefit from deep and nurturing relationships that will motivate, inspire and push them to succeed in ways they perhaps never thought possible.
Vision, Values, and Aims
Our Vision
We aspire to create an inclusive and dynamic learning environment where every child is empowered to reach their full potential. Through a commitment to excellence, personal growth, and lifelong learning, we prepare our students to thrive in an ever-changing world.
Our Values
Inclusion – Every child deserves to feel valued, supported, and respected.
Excellence – We set high expectations and strive for the best in everything we do.
Curiosity – We foster a love for learning and critical thinking.
Integrity – We foster self-awareness, emotional resilience, encouraging honesty and responsibility.
Resilience – We encourage perseverance and adaptability in the face of challenges.
Community – We build a supportive and diverse school culture where every child belongs.
Our Aims
Empower Every Child – We provide an inclusive and supportive environment where all students gain the tools, knowledge, and confidence to succeed.
Inspire Lifelong Learning – We nurture curiosity, resilience, and a passion for knowledge that extends beyond the classroom.
Deliver Excellence in Education – Through innovative teaching and a balanced curriculum, we challenge and support every student.
Promote Holistic Development – We focus on well-being, character growth, and the development of essential life skills.
Cultivate an Inclusive Community – We embrace diversity and ensure every student feels safe, valued, and heard.
Prepare for the Future – We equip students with independence, critical thinking, and adaptability to succeed in their next steps.

At Robin’s Way School, trust forms the foundation of everything we do. We prioritise building strong, supportive relationships between pupils, teachers, and the wider school community.
We recognise that each child is unique, and we tailor our education to suit their individual needs. Regardless of ability, every learning program is designed to spark a love for learning and help each pupil reach their full potential.
Our curriculum emphasises the essential skills of literacy and numeracy while ensuring that lessons are grounded in real-world relevance. This approach helps pupils connect their learning to everyday life. Alongside academics, we provide social, moral, spiritual, and cultural guidance to support their holistic development.
To broaden our pupils perspectives and aspirations, we incorporate creative experiences that extend beyond the classroom. These include educational visits and outdoor learning opportunities. Within the school, we focus on personal development and preparing children to thrive as active, responsible citizens in modern Britain.
